readme: Registry of automations + critical outputs the health-heartbeat.ps1 watches for SILENT DEATH - an automation that stopped being scheduled (deleted/disabled), or an output that quietly went stale, WITHOUT a loud failure. Since 2026-08-22 health-heartbeat runs from the 09:30 'TC Grocery Capture Watchdog' task (local-watchdog.ps1 and the SMP tasks are retired); capture-watchdog covers loud failures and the run record. Brad's rule 2026-08-22: the three 'TC Grocery *' Windows tasks are the ONLY routines that fire - every one belongs here, and health-heartbeat's REGISTRY DRIFT check pages if a 'TC *' or 'SMP *' task exists that is not listed. max_age_hours ~30 tolerates a late run + a weekend gap on a daily thing. Optional 'proves' (path or glob, repo-relative) names the output that shows the task's WORK actually landed: a nonzero exit whose proof output is fresh is reported as a warning, not paged as a death. The proof must be no older than the run it claims to prove.

windows_tasks.name: TC Grocery Ad Pulls 0700
windows_tasks.why: 07:00 weekly-ad pull for every store whose ad rolled over (capture-run -Kind ad; captures only, no chain). proves = the ads file itself: a run-log exists the moment the process starts, so proving with it downgraded a killed run (0xC000013A) to 'work landed'.

windows_tasks.name: TC Grocery Daily Capture 0800
windows_tasks.why: 08:00 quarterly-rotation capture + the ONE daily chain: compare -> guards -> publish -> recipes -> commit

windows_tasks.name: TC Grocery Capture Watchdog 0930
windows_tasks.why: 09:30 outcome check of the two tasks above (schedule, run record, board, publish, ads, browser flags) + this heartbeat. EXITS 1 BY DESIGN whenever it has findings, and it is the script that RUNS health-heartbeat - without this flag the heartbeat pages about the watchdog every day the watchdog does its job (self-referential, permanent from its first real finding).

output_files.why: public price feed every card fetches
derived item->bid map (tools + top5 badges read it; regenerated daily)
